module_specs:
  video_timing_pattern: |
    Use the 74.25 MHz pixel clock to generate CEA-861 720p60 raster timing and a stream containing RGB, positive
    horizontal and vertical sync, active-picture indication, and pixel-clock-stable indication. Generate eight
    160-pixel vertical bars in the specified order by default. Provide the one-pixel checkerboard as the other
    selectable pattern. The PATTERN register selects bars at reset and is exposed through the shell window.
  median_filter: |
    For each active output pixel, compute the median independently for each RGB channel over the 3 x 3 active-picture
    neighbourhood. At active-picture edges, extend the nearest active pixel to fill missing neighbourhood positions.
    Carry the timing and stable indications through the filter so they stay aligned with the corresponding filtered
    pixel.
  vga_output: |
    Drive the VGA RGB and sync pins from the filtered stream. Drive RGB to zero outside the active picture, while
    BTNC is pressed, or when the pixel-clock-stable indication is false. Count completed raster frames and expose the
    unsigned 32-bit count to the shell window.
  test_shell: |
    The always-present shell owns USB-UART at 115200 baud and the 0x80-0xFF register window. Use 8-N-1 ASCII lines:
    ID? returns VMED, P<n> selects a pattern, and F? returns the decimal frame counter. The shell's register window
    accesses PATTERN and FRAME_COUNT through their top-level register maps.

module_specs:
  video_timing_pattern: |
    Use the 74.25 MHz pixel clock to generate CEA-861 720p60 raster timing and a stream containing RGB, positive
    horizontal and vertical sync, active-picture indication, and pixel-clock-stable indication. Generate eight
    160-pixel vertical bars in the specified order by default. Provide the one-pixel checkerboard as the other
    selectable pattern. The PATTERN register selects bars at reset and is exposed through the shell window.
  median_filter: |
    For each active output pixel, compute the median independently for each RGB channel over the 3 x 3 active-picture
    neighbourhood. At active-picture edges, extend the nearest active pixel to fill missing neighbourhood positions.
    Carry the timing and stable indications through the filter so they stay aligned with the corresponding filtered
    pixel.
  vga_output: |
    Drive the VGA RGB and sync pins from the filtered stream. Drive RGB to zero outside the active picture, while
    BTNC is pressed, or when the pixel-clock-stable indication is false. Count completed raster frames and expose the
    unsigned 32-bit count to the shell window.
  test_shell: |
    The always-present shell owns USB-UART at 115200 baud and the 0x80-0xFF register window. Use 8-N-1 ASCII lines:
    ID? returns VMED, P<n> selects a pattern, and F? returns the decimal frame counter. The shell's register window
    accesses PATTERN and FRAME_COUNT through their top-level register maps.

    proof: [simulation, hardware]
    modules: [video_timing_pattern, top]
  - id: S-2
    text: "The default test pattern shall consist of eight vertical bars, each 160 pixels wide, ordered white, yellow, cyan, green, magenta, red, blue, and black."

  - id: S-3
    text: "For each output pixel and each colour channel, compute the median of that channel's values in the pixel's 3 x 3 neighbourhood."
    proof: [simulation, formal]
    modules: [median_filter, top]

    text: "The output picture and horizontal and vertical syncs shall remain aligned: the sync timing shall correspond to the filtered pixel positions, with the same active-picture timing and sync polarity as the timing generator."

    modules: [median_filter, vga_output, top]

    modules: [top]

    text: "Provide a test shell over the USB-UART at 115200 baud that identifies the design as VMED, allows the user to select a test pattern, and allows the user to read a frame counter."

    horizontal and vertical sync, active-picture indication, and pixel-clock-stable indication. Generate eight
    160-pixel vertical bars in the specified order by default. Provide the one-pixel checkerboard as the other

  median_filter: |
    For each active output pixel, compute the median independently for each RGB channel over the 3 x 3 active-picture

    Carry the timing and stable indications through the filter so they stay aligned with the corresponding filtered
    pixel.
  vga_output: |
    Drive the VGA RGB and sync pins from the filtered stream. Drive RGB to zero outside the active picture, while
    BTNC is pressed, or when the pixel-clock-stable indication is false. Count completed raster frames and expose the
    unsigned 32-bit count to the shell window.
  test_shell: |
    The always-present shell owns USB-UART at 115200 baud and the 0x80-0xFF register window. Use 8-N-1 ASCII lines:

  video_timing_pattern: |
    Use the 74.25 MHz pixel clock to generate CEA-861 720p60 raster timing and a stream containing RGB, positive
    horizontal and vertical sync, active-picture indication, and pixel-clock-stable indication. Generate eight
    160-pixel vertical bars in the specified order by default. Provide the one-pixel checkerboard as the other
    selectable pattern. The STATUS register is read-only, has reset value zero, and is exposed through the shell window.
  median_filter: |
    For each active output pixel, compute the median independently for each RGB channel over the 3 x 3 active-picture
    neighbourhood. At active-picture edges, extend the nearest active pixel to fill missing neighbourhood positions.
    Carry the timing and stable indications through the filter so they stay aligned with the corresponding filtered
    pixel. Sustain one beat per clock and one output beat per input beat; latency is H_TOTAL + 2 clock cycles.
  vga_output: |
    Drive the VGA RGB and sync pins from the filtered stream. Drive RGB to zero outside the active picture, while
    BTNC is pressed, or when the pixel-clock-stable indication is false. Count completed raster frames and expose the
    unsigned 32-bit count to the shell window.
  test_shell: |
    The always-present shell owns USB-UART at 115200 baud and the 0x80-0xFF register window. Use 8-N-1 ASCII lines:
    ID? returns VMED, P<n> selects a pattern, and F? returns the decimal frame counter. The shell's register window
    accesses STATUS and FRAME_COUNT through their top-level register maps.

  video_timing_pattern: |
    Use the 74.25 MHz pixel clock to generate CEA-861 720p60 raster timing and a stream containing RGB, positive
    horizontal and vertical sync, active-picture indication, and pixel-clock-stable indication. Generate eight
    160-pixel vertical bars in the specified order by default. Provide the one-pixel checkerboard as the other
    selectable pattern. The STATUS register is read-only, has reset value zero, and is exposed through the shell window.
  median_filter: |
    For each active output pixel, compute the median independently for each RGB channel over the 3 x 3 active-picture
    neighbourhood. At active-picture edges, extend the nearest active pixel to fill missing neighbourhood positions.
    Carry the timing and stable indications through the filter so they stay aligned with the corresponding filtered
    pixel. Sustain one beat per clock and one output beat per input beat; latency is H_TOTAL + 2 clock cycles.
  vga_output: |
    Drive the VGA RGB and sync pins from the filtered stream. Drive RGB to zero outside the active picture, while
    BTNC is pressed, or when the pixel-clock-stable indication is false. Count completed raster frames and expose the
    unsigned 32-bit count to the shell window.
  test_shell: |
    The always-present shell owns USB-UART at 115200 baud and the 0x80-0xFF register window. Use 8-N-1 ASCII lines:
    ID? returns VMED, P<n> selects a pattern, and F? returns the decimal frame counter. The shell's register window
    accesses STATUS and FRAME_COUNT through their top-level register maps.
